children: Amid evolving conditions in the US stock market, utility stocks remain in focus as investors assess electricity demand, infrastructure spending, and the growing need for reliable power generation and grid capacity.

Against this backdrop, utilities companies with rising capital expenditure and attractive valuations are drawing attention as investors evaluate opportunities linked to infrastructure upgrades, renewable energy projects, and expanding power-generation capacity.

The utilities sector includes businesses involved in electricity generation and distribution, natural gas services, and energy infrastructure. While higher CapEx growth can indicate increased investment in operational expansion and long-term capacity development, strong Valuation grades suggest that these stocks also screen favorably on relative valuation metrics.

Below is a list of utilities stocks ranked according to their year-over-year CapEx growth percentage, along with their Seeking Alpha Valuation ratings. All six stocks on the list carry strong Valuation grades, ranging from A to A-.
The list is topped by Clearway Energy, Inc.
, with year-over-year CapEx growth of 123.50% and a Valuation rating of A-. Brookfield Infrastructure Corporation
follows with CapEx growth of 55.42% and an A rating. Avista Corporation
ranks third with growth of 38.46% and an A- rating.
comes fourth with CapEx growth of 15.96% and an A Valuation rating, followed by Portland General Electric Company
, which recorded growth of 6.51% and carries an A- rating. The AES Corporation
rounds out the list with CapEx growth of 5.39% and an A rating.
